title: Choose Rolecall's visual world
question: The roll assigned Scorecard: your job hunt read like a live cricket scorecard. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Scorecard
options.lineage: Stadium scoreboards, the scorer's book and live ball-by-ball commentary
options.thesis: Your hunt as a live innings: every role a batting row of hard numbers, every new posting a ball called out in the commentary.
options.viewport: Landing opens on a giant scoreboard: today's new roles and India roles as hand-hung numerals, beside a live commentary column calling out fresh postings; one primary action, 'Get my scorecard'. In the app, the feed is a scorecard table: match % as the big number, skills matched, level, posted, with ball-by-ball notes as the reasons.
options.risk: Puns can drown the product: labels must stay plain English, the cricket lives in layout, numerals and rhythm, not in jokes.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: scoreboard-size numerals against tiny tabular labels, no boxes doing the work.
State is a mark in a fixed cell: saved, applied, OA, interview, offer and rejected each get one scorebook mark in the same column of every row.
Marked by hand: a saved role gets a pen ring around its number, a dismissed one is struck through, so the list remembers your triage.
Fixed anatomy: every role row shares one baseline and column order, so comparing two roles is a glance, not a read.
The focused row burns brightest while the rest recede, keeping context without competing.

options.label: Reservation Chart
options.lineage: Indian Railways reservation charts and PNR status
options.thesis: Every role carries a status you already read by heart: CNF for strong fits, RAC for stretch roles, WL for long shots.
options.viewport: Landing shows today's chart pasted on the coach: your name row with CNF/RAC/WL against fresh roles; the app feed is the chart, sorted by status.
options.risk: Strong identification, but status codes invite confusion with application status and the print look can tip into nostalgia.

options.label: Dense Board
options.thesis: Pack far more roles per screen than any Western job board: ruled modules, tiny gothic type, red tabs for new.
options.viewport: A mosaic of ruled role modules edge to edge, with a persistent filter rail and red NEW tabs.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and wins on scan speed for triage; loses on audience identification, it says efficient tool, not 'made for us'.
options.risk: Tiny type hurts on low-end phones; density must relax on mobile.

options.label: Metro Map
options.thesis: Each application is a journey along a line: saved, applied, OA, interview, offer.
options.viewport: The tracker as a line diagram; the feed as departures on a branch.
options.case: Great for the tracker, weak for the feed; both axes lose to the scorecard.
options.kept: The focused row burns brightest while the rest recede.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.case: Students don't identify with it and it hides the reasons; loses both axes.

options.label: Timetable Rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and reversal.
options.case: The rake fights reading; loses both axes.
options.kept: State as a mark in a fixed cell.

options.label: Circle Catalog
options.thesis: Thousands of postage-stamp cells, circled in biro.
options.viewport: A packed numbered grid of roles.
options.case: Foreign to the audience; thumbnails don't exist for jobs.
options.kept: Marked by hand: rings for saved, strikes for dismissed.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Each role as a plate at fixed scale.
options.viewport: Plates of roles on one baseline.
options.case: Wrong world for a job hunt; loses both axes.
options.kept: Fixed anatomy on one shared baseline.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern job board: white cards, one blue accent, rounded chips, a search bar up top.
canonCard.viewport: Search bar hero with a grid of job cards and logo tiles below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other job board by design.
